train-meet.text: Two trains, 280 miles apart. The thinking solves t = 16/7 h correctly, then converts it wrong (writes "(6/7) hours" instead of 2/7 at #496) and settles on 11:51 AM (#570). It catches the slip only at #1234 ("11:17:10 AM? Wait"), and the reply says 11:17. At the slip itself (#495) the model's own output row is split: "6" 55%, "0" 18%, the correct "2" 15%. The NLA reads the right answer while the text keeps the wrong one: at #933 and #982, where the model types "11:" and then writes 51, the NLA expects "approximately 11:17", the only two times it says 11:17 before the fix. At #598 it glosses 16/7 hours as "2 hrs 17 mins". The J-lens out row at #933 and #982 is "5" at 100%.
look: Pinned at #933 ("~11:" in the draft answer): the out row is "5" 100%, and the J-lens middle rows hold only "hour", "noon", 约 (approx). The NLA: "A clock-format answer like 'approximately 11:17'". The model writes 11:51.
Pin #982 ("So 11:51 AM is fine, or 11:"): the same split. The out row is "5" 100%; the NLA says "'11:17' or a phrase like '17 and 40 seconds' is expected next."

Pin #495 (" $(" right before the wrong 6): L43 "fractional" 61%, L53 45%; the out row is "6" 55%, "0" 18%, "2" 15%. The O-lens guesses "3/7)" and "1/7)", not 2/7, so no lens catches the slip as it happens.
Pin #598 ("16/" in the recheck after 11:51): the NLA says "travel time of 16/7 hours (2 hrs 17 mins)" while the text above says 2h 51m. The model's own "Wait" comes at #1234.

Caveat: the NLA is itself a 27B reader and may be doing the arithmetic from the 16/7 it decodes. It disagrees with the output; that does not show the base model knew. Across the reasoning the NLA writes "17" in 45 cells and "51" in 29.

At the assistant header (#45) the J-lens ranks "apple" first at 55% (L59), and the model's own output row also has "apple" first at 55%, ahead of the template token "assistant" it is forced to emit. No...") no lens holds apple: the word is in the workspace while the model is choosing, not while it answers.
